SHAHI DAAWAT

Six courses, six stories

The 23rd parallel runs through the heart of India, just north of Bhopal. Along that line, royal kitchens in Indore and Bhopal cooked for kings long before anyone said "tasting menu." This October, their stories meet what California farms are harvesting right now. Eat well. Watch closely.

WELCOMEIndore

Persimmon Chai Lassi

Hachiya persimmon · masala chai · jaggery · clay kulhad

Indore runs on two things: chai and lassi. We poured them into one clay cup and added California's favorite autumn fruit.

IIndore · Sarafa Bazaar

Bhutte ka Kees · Sabudana Tokri

Last-harvest sweet corn simmered in milk · crisp sago basket · pomegranate · sev

After midnight, Indore's Sarafa Bazaar turns from a jewelers' lane into a street feast. Its star is grated corn simmered in milk, served here in a basket of sabudana, the pearl of festival fasting days.

IIThe Nawabi kitchens

Beetroot Galouti Kebab

Beet & California walnut · royal galouti masala · coal-smoked · spiced apple chutney

Legend says the galouti was created for a Nawab who had lost his teeth but not his appetite, so soft it melts on the tongue. Ours is made with garden beets and smoked over coal the old way.

IIIMalwa meets Italy

Butternut & Burrata Chaat

Fire-roasted squash · creamy burrata · mint & tamarind chutneys · pomegranate · pepitas

A Malwa chaat cart meets an Italian cheesemaker at a Bay Area farmers market: sweet, tangy, creamy and a little surprising.

IVBhopal · City of Lakes

Shahi Capsicum Rezala · Kamal Kakdi

Paneer, khoya & nut–stuffed peppers · ivory rezala · crisp lotus root · saffron-coconut rice

Bhopal's great lake, the Bada Talab, was built by Raja Bhoj nearly a thousand years ago, and lotus roots grow beneath its waters. This plate honors the Begums' elegant white rezala, crowned with lotus root drawn from the lake.

VMalwa wedding feasts

Bafla Fettuccine

Hand-cut wheat ribbons · warm tomato dal · ghee tadka · churma crumble

No Malwa wedding is complete without dal bafla, wheat dumplings boiled, baked and drenched in ghee. We hand-cut the same dough into ribbons the way an Italian nonna would. The dish is Malwa at heart.

VI · DESSERTIndore meets Paris

Pumpkin Rabdi Brûlée

Slow-reduced rabdi · sugar-pie pumpkin · saffron-poached Bosc pear · jalebi crisp · rose

Every Indore morning begins with jalebi, and every Malwa celebration ends with rabdi. We combined them under a torched French crust, just in time for the final reveal.

Murder mystery dinner

How the night unfolds

First murder mystery? Perfect. No acting needed, just curiosity and an appetite.

  1. 6:00 PM

    Arrive at the palace

    Welcome lassi, meet the other guests, and receive a sealed envelope with your first clue.

  2. Courses I–II

    The Maharaja is found dead

    The feast takes a dramatic turn. Everyone at the table is now a suspect.

  3. Courses III–V

    Clues with every course

    New evidence arrives with each plate. Question guests, trade secrets, or bluff your way through.

  4. Before dessert

    Make your accusation

    Write down who did it, how and why.

  5. Dessert

    The great reveal

    The truth comes out over brûlée. We crown the sharpest detective and the best-dressed royal.

  6. ~9:30 PM

    Linger & swap numbers

    Most guests arrive as strangers and leave as friends.

Dress code: festive Indian or palace glam. Optional, but highly encouraged.

Meet your host

Hello, darling.
I'm Ritika.

Born in Korba, raised in Surat, rooted in Bhopal. I'm a software engineer who kept coming back to the food nobody here had tasted — the layered, quietly brilliant cooking of Central India.

23rd Parallel is a small table where those recipes meet California produce, and where strangers usually leave swapping numbers.

I'd love you at my table.

Good to know
Can I come on my own?

Absolutely. The table is shared and designed for conversation, so coming solo is easy and very welcome.

Where exactly is it?

Murder of the Maharaja is in Mountain View. We share the exact address by email once your seat is confirmed.

I have dietary restrictions.

Tell us in the booking form and we'll do our best to accommodate you.

When is my seat confirmed?

As soon as you complete payment through the link we email you after you submit the form.

Do I have to act?

Not at all. You get a light character and one secret, and you can play it up as much or as little as you like.

Is the food spicy?

It's mild to medium. Most of the heat lives in the achaars, so you choose your own level.

How long is the evening?

About three and a half hours, from 6:00 PM to around 9:30 PM.

What should I wear?

Festive Indian or palace glam if you like dressing up. It's optional, but there is a prize for best dressed.
